answer: Provenance spiral ledger. Each identity must append a fresh, verifiable work record whose input includes the prior record’s full hash, forming a per-identity hash chain. A sparrow-level check samples any chain and replays it; duplicates collapse because copied records share ancestry. A comet mark—a rare, costly banded artifact seeded unpredictably—must appear once per chain at an unknown depth, forcing attackers to solve and store unique chains per identity. Cost: one full recomputation and storage per sybil, plus lost work when a collision is caught.
